title: Module 3 Challenge: What Does the Correlation Tell You?
scenario: A researcher studying 40 undergraduates reports r = +.45 between weekly hours of social media use and self-reported loneliness. A news site writes: "Social media makes students lonely. The study found that 45 percent of loneliness comes from social media use."

parts.q: What proportion of variability in loneliness is accounted for by social media use in this linear relationship?
Which statement about the direction of this relationship is correct?
o: Students who use more social media tend to report more loneliness
Students who use more social media report less loneliness
Social media use has no connection to loneliness
parts.why: The positive sign means the two variables rise together on average.

parts.q: The headline makes two errors. Identify each, and write a corrected one-sentence summary of what the study actually found.
parts.model: The first error is the causal claim. A correlation of .45 from a survey cannot show that social media causes loneliness. Lonely students may turn to social media more, or a third variable such as stress could affect both. The second error is treating r as a percentage. The proportion of shared variability is r squared, .45 squared = about .20, so about 20 percent of the variability in loneliness is linked to social media use. A corrected statement is "Across 40 students, more hours of social media use went along with higher loneliness, and the two variables shared about 20 percent of their variability."
check: I rejected the causal claim and named a reverse direction or third variable
I corrected 45 percent to r squared, about 20 percent
My rewrite described association rather than cause
